newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Clashes over local polls in Senegalese town.
newsitem.headline: Clashes over local polls in Senegalese town.

text.p: Opposition supporters clashed with riot police firing tear gas in the Senegalese town of Saint Louis on Wednesday during a protest calling for a re-run of local elections held at the start of the week, witnesses said.

The protest took place as the capital Dakar held new polls after Sunday's chaotic municipal elections during which organisational chaos prevented many people from voting, particularly in the Dakar suburbs.

Witnesses told Reuters by telephone from the northern town of Saint Louis that many opposition supporters -- demonstrating in favour of holding another vote -- had been arrested and at least one person had been hurt by the tear gas. They gave no figure for the arrests.
The main opposition Senegalese Democratic Party (PDS), which has called for the results nationwide of Sunday's poll to be scrapped, nevertheless took part in the Dakar re-runs.
Results from other areas have yet to be formally declared.
PDS leader Abdoulaye Wade, defeated by President Abdou Diouf in disputed presidential elections in 1993, was running for the job of mayor of the capital Dakar.
The ruling Socialist Party was trying on Sunday to recapture the urban vote, which it lost to the opposition during presidential and parliamentary polls in 1993.
The opposition boycotted the last municipal polls that took place in 1989 before Senegal's transition to more open multi-party politics.
Fourteen political parties were contesting seats on regional, municipal, district and rural councils on Sunday. Just over three million people were eligible to vote then.
